title: Chart.js Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Chart.js course.

entries.name: Create a bar chart
entries.summary: A bar chart compares amounts between categories.

entries.name: Name a dataset
entries.summary: A dataset label explains what a set of values measures.

entries.name: Use a line for ordered change
entries.summary: A line chart can show how a value changes across an ordered sequence, such as days.

entries.name: Show parts of one total
entries.summary: A doughnut chart shows shares of a total.

entries.name: Plot pairs with a scatter chart
entries.summary: A scatter chart places each item using an x value and a y value.

entries.name: Choose an honest baseline
entries.summary: A bar's length should make comparisons clear.

entries.name: Compare two datasets
entries.summary: Two datasets can share the same categories.

entries.name: Update data without making a new chart
entries.summary: A chart instance can receive changed data.

entries.name: Fit a sized container
entries.summary: A responsive chart uses its parent container to decide its display size.

entries.name: Turn off unnecessary animation
entries.summary: Chart animation can be disabled when it is not useful.

entries.name: Provide text outside the canvas
entries.summary: Canvas drawings do not contain normal readable HTML rows.

entries.name: Destroy an unused chart
entries.summary: A chart can keep event listeners and drawing resources.
